items.quote: Easy Setup: Quick to create and share with no technical expertise required.
items.comment: Change to “Easy Setup: Create and share a link in minutes, with no technical expertise required.”

items.reason: The sentence is passive, and the style guide prefers “payment” to “transaction”.

items.comment: Change to “Product Listings: Merchants can list multiple products with images, descriptions, and prices on their social media profiles.”

items.comment: Change to “Customers can click a product listing and complete the purchase”

items.quote: Marketing Reach

items.quote: Here are the main features of QR Code:

items.quote: Contactless Payments: Supports safe, touch-free transactions.
items.comment: Change “transactions” to “payments”
items.reason: The style guide prefers “payment” to “transaction”.

items.comment: Change the labels “Easy to Use” and “Versatile” to noun phrases such as “Simple Setup” and “Wide Use”
items.reason: Parallelism. Three labels are noun phrases (“Contactless Payments”, “Secure Transactions”, “No Extra Hardware Needed”) and two are adjectives.

items.quote: Secure Transactions: Payments are processed through PayPal's platform.
items.comment: Change to “Secure Payments: PayPal processes every payment securely.”
items.reason: The label says “Transactions” but the sentence says “Payments”, and the sentence is passive.

items.quote: help protect both merchant and customers from fraud

items.reason: The sentence is passive.

items.quote: Select Help
items.comment: Use one verb for all four steps, for example “Select”, and format “Help”, “Delete Profile” and “Confirm” in bold
items.reason: The list mixes “Select” and “Click” for the same kind of action, and the style guide says clickable actions are formatted in bold.

screens.lesson: Lesson 10 of 12 — Product Availability by Region

items.quote: Product Availability by Region
items.comment: Delete this heading
items.reason: The lesson title directly above already says “Product Availability by Region”.

items.quote: Product / Feature
items.comment: Add a lead line above the table, for example “Use the table below to check which products are available in a merchant’s region.”
items.reason: The style guide requires a lead line that connects an element to the surrounding content. The table appears with no introduction.

items.quote: APAC
items.comment: Remove the 🌏 and 🌎 emoji from the APAC and LATAM headings, or add matching emoji to U.S. and U.K. / EMEA
items.reason: Two of the four region headings carry an emoji and two do not.

items.quote: PayPal Business Account
items.comment: Change “PayPal Business Account” to “PayPal business account”
items.reason: The style guide says to lowercase “business account”.

items.quote: Expanded Checkout (ACDC/PPCP)
items.comment: Spell out ACDC and PPCP, or remove them
items.reason: Neither acronym is explained anywhere in the module.

screens.lesson: Lesson 10 of 12 — Product Availability by Region

items.quote: Sell on Social (FB/ Instagram)
items.comment: Change to “Sell on Social (Facebook and Instagram)”
items.reason: There is a stray space after the slash, and “FB” is an informal abbreviation. Lesson 3 writes both names in full.

items.quote: Subscriptions/Smart Subscribe
items.comment: Introduce Smart Subscribe in Lesson 4, or remove it from this table
items.reason: Smart Subscribe appears only here and is never explained.

items.quote: US Only
items.comment: Change “US Only” to “U.S. only”
items.reason: The column heading uses “U.S.” with periods, and “only” does not need a capital.

items.quote: UK + select EU
items.comment: Change “UK + select EU” to “U.K. and select EU markets”, and “MX + BR only” to “Mexico and Brazil only”
items.reason: The table mixes full country names, two-letter codes and plus signs for the same kind of information.

items.quote: Withdrawn 2023
items.comment: Correct either this row or the note in Lesson 2 — this table shows Zettle withdrawn in the U.S. and available in Mexico and Brazil, while Lesson 2 says Zettle is available in the U.S. and was withdrawn from Brazil
items.reason: The two lessons state opposite facts. The U.S. and Brazil entries appear to have been swapped.

items.quote: Standard/Legacy Buttons (WPS)
items.comment: Spell out WPS, or remove it
items.reason: The acronym is not explained anywhere in the module.

items.quote: PayPal Payments Pro/ VT 2.0
items.comment: Change to “PayPal Payments Pro and Virtual Terminal 2.0”
items.reason: There is a stray space after the slash and “VT” is not defined.

items.quote: Legacy product
items.comment: Change “✅ Legacy product” to “⚠️ Legacy product”
items.reason: “Legacy product” is not an availability status, and the green tick tells the learner the product is fully available.

screens.lesson: Lesson 10 of 12 — Product Availability by Region

items.quote: TBC = To Be Confirmed with regional product owners before curriculum launch
items.comment: Change to “TBC = to be confirmed”
items.reason: “With regional product owners before curriculum launch” is a note to the course team, not to the learner.

items.quote: Select markets
items.comment: Use a different symbol for “TBC” than for “Select markets”
items.reason: The same warning symbol marks both, so the legend does not tell the two apart.

items.quote: Not available
items.comment: Replace the green, pink and amber cell fills with the brand palette, or use symbols and text on a white background
items.reason: The green (#E8F5E9), pink and amber fills are not in the brand palette (White #FFFFFF, Black #000000, PayPal Blue #003087, Bright Blue #60CDFF).

items.quote: TBC
items.comment: Check the contrast of the orange “TBC” text on the amber fill and the red “Not available” text on the pink fill
items.reason: These colour combinations look below the 4.5:1 minimum contrast ratio for body text.

items.quote: This quiz will test how well you can support Products Deep Dive.
items.comment: Change to “This quiz will test how well you can support merchants with PayPal products.”
items.reason: “Products Deep Dive” is the name of the module, not something a learner supports.

items.quote: This quiz comprises 5 questions.
items.comment: Change “This quiz comprises 5 questions.” to “Answer all five questions”
items.reason: Two problems. Parallelism — the other two bullets are instructions while this one is a statement. Also numbers one to nine are spelled out.

items.quote: Read each question carefully.
items.comment: Remove the full stops from all three bullets
items.reason: The style guide says bulleted lists in training modules should not end with periods.

prep.text: key benefit of PayPal No Code

items.quote: PayPal No Code Solutions
items.comment: Change “No Code Solutions” to “No-Code Solutions”
items.reason: Lesson 3 hyphenates it. The same change is needed in the Question 3 options.

items.quote: Supports only cash transactions
items.comment: Change “cash transactions” to “cash payments”
items.reason: The style guide says to use “payment” rather than “transaction”.

screens.screen: Question — “Which PayPal product allows customers to split payments into installments?”

items.quote: APIs & Integration
items.comment: Change “APIs & Integration” to “APIs and Integrations”
items.reason: The style guide says to avoid ampersands in web text, and the lesson itself is called “API and Integration”.

items.quote: Shopping Cart
items.comment: Replace “Shopping Cart” with a PayPal product covered in the module, such as “Subscriptions”
items.reason: Shopping Cart is not one of the products taught, so it is not a fair answer option.

screens.screen: Question — “What is the primary purpose of PayPal APIs and Integrations?” and feedback

items.quote: Managing employee payroll
items.comment: Change “Managing employee payroll” to “To manage employee payroll”
items.reason: Parallelism. The other three options start with “To” plus a verb; this one starts with a gerund.

items.quote: What is the primary purpose of PayPal APIs and Integrations?
items.comment: Use one name for this topic across the module — “APIs and Integrations”
items.reason: The lesson is called “API and Integration”, a Question 3 option says “APIs & Integration”, and this question says “APIs and Integrations”.

items.quote: correct response
items.comment: Add specific feedback for each question explaining why the answer is right or wrong
items.reason: Every question shows the same generic message, so a learner who answers incorrectly is told nothing that helps them learn.

items.quote: You should be able to:
items.comment: Change “You should be able to:” to “You should now be able to:”
items.reason: The style guide sets this exact wrap-up phrase. The word “now” is missing.

items.quote: Click the EXIT MODULE button to close the training.
items.comment: Format “EXIT MODULE” in bold
items.reason: The style guide says clickable actions are formatted in bold.

other.title: Two different table header colours across the curriculum
other.text: The Lesson 10 table header uses PayPal Blue #003087, which is correct. The top navigation bar uses #0070CC and the In-Person Payments with PayPal module uses #008CFF for its table headers. Neither of those is in the brand palette (White #FFFFFF, Black #000000, PayPal Blue #003087, Bright Blue #60CDFF). Standardise on #003087.

other.title: Tab labels are set in ALL CAPS
other.text: Tab labels render as “PAY LINKS”, “SELL ON SOCIAL”, “QR CODE”, “CLASSIC API” and “REST API”. The style guide reserves ALL CAPS for acronyms and job titles.

other.title: Product lessons are uneven in depth
other.text: In Person Payments, No-Code Solutions and Subscriptions each have a description, pain points, benefits and a note. PayPal Pay Later has no pain points, and Virtual Terminal has only a description and a screenshot. Consider a consistent structure for every product lesson.

other.title: Lesson 7 API flow does not match Lesson 8
other.text: Lesson 7 gives a four-step API flow that ends at buyer approval. Lesson 8 gives a four-step flow that ends at capture. The two are describing the same process and should agree.

other.title: No lead line before the Classic API / REST API tabs
other.text: Lesson 3 correctly introduces its tabs with “Click the tabs below…”. The tabs in Lesson 7 appear with no lead line, which the style guide requires.

other.title: Authoring notes left in the published module
other.text: Three pieces of text address the course team rather than the learner: “so confirm availability before publishing” (Lesson 3), “Why this matters in training…” (Lesson 8), and “TBC = To Be Confirmed with regional product owners before curriculum launch” (Lesson 10).

other.title: Cross-module consistency
other.text: This module writes “In Person Payments” without a hyphen; the In-Person Payments with PayPal module hyphenates it. This module’s quiz says “from the options below”; the other says “from the list below”. Both modules omit “now” from the wrap-up phrase, and neither expands “BRE”.

other.title: Video playback could not be verified
other.text: The self-hosted MP4 videos would not play in the audit browser, although the files themselves are served correctly. This is a limitation of the audit environment, not a defect in the module. Please confirm playback manually.
